title: Self-Hosting Foundation and Compiler Subset Contract
purpose: Define the first BASIC# subset allowed for future compiler-writing work while Ruby remains the bootstrap compiler and reference authority.

small compiler subset symbol table contract under Ruby referee
small compiler subset BSBC emission under Ruby referee

independent Subset 0 BSBC validation through SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCLoader under production BytecodeLoader referee parity
independent Subset 0 BSBC execution through SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCVirtualMachine under production BytecodeVirtualMachine and Ruby Runtime referee parity
integrated Subset 0 source-to-world orchestration through SmallCompilerSubsetPipeline while production compiler components and Ruby Runtime remain separate referees
first BASIC#-authored compiler-domain decision component compiled to real BSBC and executed by the independent BSharp VM under separate production and Ruby referees

self_hosting_sequence.goal: Record the rejected v0.0.43 package, then freeze this foundation contract and validation gate.
Build a BASIC# tokenizer/reader contract and fixture set before implementation.
Implement tokenizer/reader pieces with Ruby as referee and compare deterministic records.
Parse a small approved compiler subset into deterministic records under Ruby Parser referee.
Emit BSharp IR from small compiler subset records under Ruby Parser plus SemanticResolver referee.
Lock golden IR parity for the small compiler subset.
Lock plain-English error records for invalid small compiler subset examples.
Expand the small compiler subset across larger scene/block fixtures under Ruby referee.
Emit BSBC from BASIC# compiler code and require byte-for-byte parity before replacing Ruby.
Give BSharp Compiler Subset 0 its own semantic resolver implementation and require exact BSharp IR parity against the production Ruby SemanticResolver referee.
Give BSharp Compiler Subset 0 its own BSBC encoder and require exact byte-for-byte parity against the production Ruby BytecodeEmitter referee.
Give BSharp Compiler Subset 0 its own BSBC loader trust boundary and require exact valid-model plus malformed-artifact rejection parity against the production Ruby BytecodeLoader referee.
Give BSharp Compiler Subset 0 its own BSBC execution engine and require exact production-VM and Ruby-runtime parity across Profiles 1 through 7.

Connect the bounded reader, parser, semantic resolver, BSharp IR, independent BSBC encoder, independent BSBC loader, and independent BSharp VM into one integrated source-to-world compiler pipeline under separate Ruby referee parity.

Place an independent compiler driver in front of SmallCompilerSubsetPipeline, persist real BSBC artifacts, reload them through SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCLoader, and execute them through SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCVirtualMachine while production compiler components and Ruby Runtime remain separate referees.

Author the first bounded compiler-domain decision component in BASIC#, compile it through SmallCompilerSubsetDriver into real BSBC, and execute it source-free through the independent loader and BSharp VM under separate production and Ruby referee parity.

Route bounded parser block-Head dispatch through the accepted BASIC#-authored BSBC compiler component, require visible no-fallback sabotage failure, observable invocation counts, and a byte-identical two-generation bootstrap fixed point.

Route bounded semantic-family decisions through a BASIC#-authored BSBC semantic component, preserve v0.0.81 native parser dispatch upstream, require wrong-route fail-closed sabotage, observable invocation counts, and a byte-identical two-generation bootstrap fixed point.

Route bounded Kind, Thing, PLAYER, action, value, duplicate, unknown, and Kind-link symbol decisions through a BASIC#-authored BSBC symbol component, preserve v0.0.81 parser dispatch and v0.0.82 semantic routing upstream, require fail-closed sabotage, observable invocation counts, exact referee parity, and a byte-identical two-generation fixed point.

Route every accepted official action word through a BASIC#-authored BSBC action-family classifier, preserve v0.0.81-v0.0.83 native stages, require fail-closed wrong-family sabotage, observable invocation counts, exact referee parity, and a byte-identical fixed point.
